_comment: Model failure classification + recovery. More mature than a naive 'fall back on any error': each error class decides whether to retry (with exponential backoff), fall back, shrink scope, fix credentials, or abort — and the fallback chain forbids downgrading to a model that cannot do the task.

error_classes.action: exponential backoff (wait base * factor^n before the n-th retry) on the SAME model; if it persists past max_retries, fall back to the next model
switch provider or model — never retry the same model, it will not succeed
shrink the scope (one file, one sink class) or fall back to a longer-context model — retrying the same prompt will fail again
retry once with a smaller scope; if it persists, fall back to the next model
retry with backoff, then fall back to the next model in the chain
fix the credentials — neither retry nor fall back will help
retry with backoff; if persistent, fall back to the next model
retry with backoff; if persistent, fall back to the next model
fix the permission or scope — neither retry nor fall back will help
retry immediately — the abort is likely a transient signal, not a model failure

fallback_chain: prefer the same provider's fallback model first (e.g. deepseek-v4-pro -> deepseek-v4-flash)
then a different provider with the same capability
never fall back to a model that cannot do the task (do not send deep reasoning to a small model)

backoff.note: wait base * factor^n seconds before the n-th retry; give up (or fall back) after max_retries
